clue.text: Takes for granted while South American accommodates me

parts.note: 'as' can mean while, at the same time that

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to house them, so one piece lodges inside the other

parts.note: S for South plus US for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone presumes things while a Latin American friend puts them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one person but splits into S and US, which then takes in ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose something is true without proof, which is taking it for granted.

clue.text: Film star in part (not the lead)

indicators.note: the lead is what goes in front, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a factor is one part or element of something

explanation.surface: A screen star has only a supporting role, not the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like casting news but tells you to drop the first letter of the word for 'part'.
explanation.definitionFit: A film star is a performer in movies, which is what an actor is.

clue.text: Agile and artful seizing power? Correct

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, so one piece is clutched within the other

parts.note: sly means cunning or artful
P is the symbol for power
right means correct

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone nimble and crafty is right to grab power.
explanation.walkthrough: SLY takes in P followed by RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy, so nimble or agile in movement.

clue.text: Security camera shows fool breaking anchor

indicators.note: something breaking into another gets inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to moor a boat is to anchor it
nit is short for nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: CCTV footage shows an idiot damaging a ship's anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a device that keeps watch, and a CCTV screen or camera system is one such example.

clue.text: Have views about awful quarters round centre of Seattle where there's adverse possession

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the jumbled word wraps the next piece
about here means surrounding, so the views word goes around everything else

parts.note: sights are views; to have them is to see

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so these letters are messed up

parts.note: the letters of quarters, rearranged

indicators.note: the centre is the very middle, so only the midpoint letter of the city is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of Seattle

explanation.surface: Someone with opinions on dreadful lodgings in central Seattle, a place where property is held without title.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged quarters wraps round T, and that whole lot sits inside SIGHTS after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse possession is the legal doctrine by which long occupation of land without title can become ownership, popularly called squatters' rights.

clue.text: Tried it? Politician was first

parts.note: 'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, SA
Member of Parliament
to lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: A question about whether a politician tried something, answered by saying they were the first to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried it?' reads as one phrase, but 'Tried' alone is the definition and 'it' supplies SA, short for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample something is to try or taste a little of it.

clue.text: President's address?

parts.note: surface reading: where the president lives, his home address
setter's reading: the speech the US president gives to Congress each year on how the nation is doing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' first suggests a postal location; the question mark tells you it is a formal speech instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual report by the US president to Congress is formally a message, delivered as a speech, so it is the president's best-known address.

clue.text: See 5
Cable on river vessel

parts.note: a cable is a line
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A cable is strung along a river boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Penny, old model, caught in act and put away

indicators.note: someone caught in the act is trapped within it, so the first pieces go inside the word for act

parts.note: a deed is an act
P is the abbreviation for a penny
O is the abbreviation for old
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A former model named Penny was caught in the act and sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like the model's name; it is just P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deposited has been placed somewhere for safekeeping, that is, put away.

clue.text: Natural at spinning, a spider

indicators.note: spinning turns things round and round, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: A spider is a born natural at spinning webs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' fits the spider picture perfectly, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy kind of spider, so this is an example-to-class definition.

clue.text: First light and star's out of bed

parts.note: the sun is a star; the 's stands for 'is', a joining word
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: At dawn a celebrity is already out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment of sunrise, when daylight first appears.

clue.text: Unexpected treasures sought in reference book

indicators.note: unexpected things turn up in a surprising order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Unexpected riches are being looked for in a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: A thesaurus is a 'treasury' of words, so the treasures are a neat nod to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's Thesaurus is the classic English dictionary of synonyms, a standard work consulted for words.

clue.text: Released group without charge

parts.note: a set is a group
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A band of people was released without being charged with a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without charge' suggests a police release, but here it simply means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone free is to release or liberate them.

clue.text: Last of contractors to fly over to knock down part of factory

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of contractors
to hop over somewhere is to fly there for a short trip
to floor someone is to knock them down

explanation.surface: The final contractors fly in to demolish a section of a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The shop floor is the production area of a factory where the work is done, as against the offices.

clue.text: Goods about to be placed in box

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: to box is to fight
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Merchandise is about to be packed into a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container noun but is the verb, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo, the goods carried by a ship, lorry or train.

clue.text: Popular as an ingredient of pineapple syrup

indicators.note: an ingredient goes inside the mixture, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: pineapple is old military slang for a hand grenade
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A well-liked ingredient of a pineapple-flavoured syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: The pineapple seems to belong to the syrup, but it is the slang name for a ridged hand grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red cordial syrup, traditionally flavoured with pomegranate.

clue.text: Work across extremely lofty face of major mountain

indicators.note: lying across something spans it on both sides, so the work word straddles the other pieces

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially a musical one

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: the outermost letters of lofty

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the front letter of major

explanation.surface: A climbing route crosses the steep face of a big mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the Latin word for a composition, which is split open to hold the other letters; 'face' sounds like a cliff face but is just the front letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympus is the highest mountain in Greece, home of the gods in myth.

clue.text: Breaking the tape, something that one especially dislikes

indicators.note: something broken falls apart, so the letters following are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Winning a race by breaking the finishing tape is something someone loathes.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking the tape is what a race winner does, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate is a particular thing a person finds especially irritating, the opposite of a favourite.

clue.text: Headstrong type, easily made angry by principal

parts.note: hot as in hot-tempered
the head is the principal of a school; 'by' just places it next

explanation.surface: A rash person is quick to anger, as the head teacher discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is an impetuous, rash person who acts without thinking, much like someone headstrong.

clue.text: Time and cause of betrayal

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: Questioning when and why someone was betrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: US army officer in fräulein's tent playing with it

indicators.note: playing around with something messes it up, so these letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, umlaut dropped
taken as written; 'with' adds it to the rest

explanation.surface: An American officer is in a German woman's tent, fooling around with something.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Army a first lieutenant is the junior commissioned rank above second lieutenant.

clue.text: Call about superior feeling remorse

indicators.note: about here means around, so the call word surrounds the superior letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
U means upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: A phone call about a boss who is regretting something.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it bitterly, so ruing is feeling remorse.

clue.text: Giant bird given a name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An enormous bird has been named.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of great size or power, from the giant deities of Greek myth.

clue.text: Something to raise spirits? Yes, used in France and Germany

parts.note: the French for yes
the German for yes

explanation.surface: A cheering remedy is approved in two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise spirits' sounds like cheering someone up; the question mark points to summoning ghosts instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is used at seances to try to contact the dead, so it raises spirits in the ghostly sense.

clue.text: Worn as a penance by beast with rishi, possibly, inside

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the garment rather than a noun

indicators.note: inside says the sage's jumbled letters sit within the animal word
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: a rishi is a Hindu sage; its letters are rearranged
a hart is a male deer

explanation.surface: Something is worn in penance by an animal that has a holy man inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair shirt is a rough garment of goat hair worn by ascetics to mortify the flesh.

clue.text: Go back with registrar on steamship

parts.note: a common abbreviation of registrar
re means on the subject of
the usual prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Someone sails home with the registrar aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like it means aboard, but it is RE, as in 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to return to an earlier state, literally to move backward.

clue.text: Grandmother eager to acquire cotton cloth

parts.note: nan is a familiar British name for a grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Granny is keen to buy some cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing, China.
